entry.title: DUNE far detector
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. Construction of the detector modules has started nearly a mile underground in South Dakota. Crews from Fermilab, CERN and SURF are assembling large steel beams for the outer structure, and teams are beginning the cryostats that will house approximately 17,000 tons of liquid argon. A separate Fermilab report describes the Long-Baseline Neutrino Facility construction as entering its next phase, with critical components arriving.

entry.title: DUNE collaboration and near detector
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. Black Hills State University became an institutional member of DUNE, which now counts more than 1,500 collaborators from 228 institutions in 38 countries and CERN. The collaboration also released a simulation-based sensitivity study of the near detector to eV-scale sterile neutrinos in the 3+1 framework. It uses three samples: highly elastic muon-neutrino and electron-neutrino charged-current events, and neutrino-electron elastic scattering, chosen to reduce interaction and flux uncertainties.

entry.title: SBND first results
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. The Short-Baseline Near Detector collaboration released its first neutrino results after years of preparation. The result improves neutrino interaction modelling, which Fermilab presents as groundwork for DUNE. Separately, SLAC's machine-learning reconstruction tool SPINE, which turns detector images into reconstructed neutrino interactions, is deployed in the SBN programme and in DUNE.

entry.title: IceCube Galactic plane
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. IceCube presented the first measurement of the variation of the high-energy neutrino flux along the Galactic plane, using 10 years of shower data. The fit leaves both normalisation and spectral index free in several regions, independent of model expectations. The spectral indices are 2.76 (+0.18, −0.15) in the inner region and 3.13 (+0.57, −0.37) in the outer region. The collaboration also held its fall meeting in Madison with more than 230 participants.

entry.title: KM3NeT and ANTARES
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. A new paper reports searches for coincident gravitational waves and high-energy neutrinos with KM3NeT and ANTARES data from the O3 observing run. It describes how joint observations of neutrinos and gravitational waves from the same sources were sought. The KM3NeT Collaboration also held its autumn 2026 meeting in Siracusa, with an agenda that included status updates on detector operations.

entry.title: Askaryan Radio Array
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. The ARA Collaboration published its first array-wide search for diffuse ultrahigh-energy neutrinos, using all five stations and 10.6 years of livetime, three times more than previous ARA searches. It found no events on an expected background of 0.13 ± 0.01 (stat.) (+0.05, −0.06) (syst.). The resulting upper limit is the most stringent from 50 EeV to 1000 EeV and gives the first constraints on the flux reported by KM3NeT. A companion paper details the analysis methodology.

entry.title: Neutrino telescope network
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. A projection study considers X-ray-bright Seyfert galaxies as neutrino sources, using a network of IceCube, Baikal-GVD, KM3NeT/ARCA and P-ONE. In an AGN-corona emission model, it finds the Circinus Galaxy to be the most promising point-source target in the Southern sky. It would be detected at the 5σ level by 2038 at the latest, under assumptions about the Seyfert population's contribution to the diffuse flux.

entry.title: NINJA FROST tracker
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. A meter-scale scintillator tracker with embedded scatterers, FROST, was built and operated in the NINJA experiment to match muon tracks between the nuclear emulsion detectors and the downstream muon detector. During J-PARC neutrino-beam operation it reached a data acquisition efficiency of 99.59% and a detection efficiency of 99.946 ± 0.006% for selected neutrino-induced muons well within the active area.

entry.title: The paper studies the neutrino emissivity of Δ-direct-Urca processes in neutron-star cores, where Δ isobars ma
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. The paper studies the neutrino emissivity of Δ-direct-Urca processes in neutron-star cores, where Δ isobars may appear alongside nucleons and hyperons. Urca processes are dominant neutrino-cooling channels, so this contribution matters for models of neutron-star thermal evolution.

entry.title: The authors present semianalytic approximations for the quasisteady outcome of slow and fast flavour conversio
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. The authors present semianalytic approximations for the quasisteady outcome of slow and fast flavour conversion in quasihomogeneous neutrino ensembles with periodic boundary conditions. The ansatz agrees well with multiangle and multienergy solutions of the kinetic equations and does not depend on the mass ordering. It offers a possible subgrid scheme for supernova simulations that cannot include neutrino quantum kinetics.

entry.title: The paper proves a no-go theorem: any completely positive trace-preserving evolution covariant under rotations
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. The paper proves a no-go theorem: any completely positive trace-preserving evolution covariant under rotations of the mass-coherence plane is exactly blind to a Majorana phase in two-flavour oscillations. A rate anisotropy can act as an environmental phase reference and restore sensitivity. This shows when decoherence could, and could not, reveal a Majorana phase.

entry.title: The authors derive exclusion limits on six anomaly-free U(1)_X dark photon models, with kinetic and mass mixin
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. The authors derive exclusion limits on six anomaly-free U(1)_X dark photon models, with kinetic and mass mixing, from solar neutrino-electron scattering in PandaX-4T and XENONnT. The stringency of the limits correlates with the leptonic charge assignments of each model. They also give model-independent limits for pure kinetic and pure mass mixing.

entry.title: The paper uses an ultralight vector boson from a gauged L_μ − L_τ symmetry, which modifies solar-neutrino osci
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. The paper uses an ultralight vector boson from a gauged L_μ − L_τ symmetry, which modifies solar-neutrino oscillations through an effective matter potential via kinetic mixing. It draws on recent measurements from Borexino, SNO and Super-Kamiokande and discusses prospects for JUNO and XLZD.

entry.title: The authors investigate whether kiloton-scale detectors such as Hyper-Kamiokande could measure the primary cos
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. The authors investigate whether kiloton-scale detectors such as Hyper-Kamiokande could measure the primary cosmic-ray spectrum through the atmospheric neutrino flux. They argue that future detectors can distinguish between cosmic-ray models with high statistical significance, even allowing for cross-section and hadronic-interaction uncertainties. They also introduce a technique for reconstructing the primary spectrum.
